findings.title: A compiled program killed by a signal makes `--run` exit 255 with no message at all
findings.why: runCmd collapses "could not start" and "killed by a signal" into -1, and main passes that straight out as its own exit status, which the C runtime truncates to 255 (`return runCmd(runArgv);`, main.c:657). The parent prints nothing in that case -- no `WIFSIGNALED`/`WTERMSIG` report, no one-line note -- so a generated program that segfaults under `--run` is indistinguishable from one that called exit(255), and the documented promise that the compiler never produces undefined behaviour cannot be told apart from a genuine crash. Verified: a null-reference dereference (`*p!`) compiles cleanly (exit 0) and then `--run` exits 255 with empty stderr.
findings.trigger: Any program whose process is terminated by a signal (SIGSEGV, SIGABRT, SIGFPE, ...) while running under `--run`.
findings.repro:
cat > /tmp/t_crash.extc <<'EOF'
fn main() -> i32 {
    var p: ?ref i32 = null
    return *p!
}
EOF
/home/alphayang/extC_Compiler/build/extc /tmp/t_crash.extc; echo "compile=$?"        # 0
timeout 30 /home/alphayang/extC_Compiler/build/extc --run /tmp/t_crash.extc 2>/tmp/cr.err; echo "run=$?"   # 255
wc -c /tmp/cr.err                                                                     # 0 bytes, no diagnostic

findings.title: `--help` (documented as listing every accepted switch) omits `--explain-memory`, which the driver accepts
findings.why: usage() (main.c:146-183) enumerates -o, --run, --check-c, -w, -I, -O0..-O3, -march=native, --dump-tokens, --dump-effects, --no-line-map and -h/--help, but never --explain-memory, even though the driver accepts it here and docs/EXTC-SHOWCASE.md:47 uses it as a user-facing command. The comment above usage() calls the text "the only documentation the driver ships" and claims it lists every accepted switch; tools/check_switches.py only ratchets the EXTC_* environment variables, so nothing catches this gap. A user cannot discover the flag from the compiler itself.
findings.trigger: `extc --help` (or -h); the flag is also missing from README/docs' command synopsis.

findings.title: $CC is exec'd as one program path, so a conventional `CC="cc -m32"` (or `ccache cc`) cannot be used by --run or --check-c
findings.why: `cc` comes from `getenv("CC")` (main.c:605) and is passed as argv[0] to execvp, so any arguments embedded in $CC become part of the program name. The child then fails with `extc: cannot exec `cc -m32`: No such file or directory` and the parent reports `extc: C compiler failed (exit 127)`, which names neither $CC nor the shell-quoting problem. The same single-string assumption is used for the --check-c invocation (main.c:544). $CC values with flags are the norm in make/ninja/CI setups, so this is a common configuration rejected with a misleading message.
findings.trigger: `CC` set to anything with a space in it, e.g. `CC="cc -m32"`, `CC="ccache cc"`, `CC="gcc -std=gnu11"`, together with `--run` or `--check-c`.
findings.repro:
cd /tmp/extc-t && CC="cc -m32" /home/alphayang/extC_Compiler/build/extc --run t_hyg.extc; echo $?
# -> extc: cannot exec `cc -m32`: No such file or directory
#    extc: C compiler failed (exit 127) on `build/t_hyg.c`

findings.title: `-o FILE` is silently ignored when `--run` is also given: the requested output file is never written and no error is reported
findings.why: The whole -o handling lives inside `if (!doRun)`, so under --run the driver writes only build/<base>.c and never mentions that outPath was dropped. The option parser accepts both flags without complaint (main.c:370-372 and 362-363), and usage() describes -o unconditionally, so an explicit request is discarded silently -- a build script that adds --run to an existing `-o` command line stops producing the C file it used to read, with exit status 0.
findings.trigger: `extc --run -o out.c prog.extc` (or `--dump-tokens -o out.c`, which returns before the !doRun block at main.c:415-424 and likewise writes nothing).
findings.repro:
cd /tmp/extc-t && rm -f /tmp/should_be_written.c
timeout 60 /home/alphayang/extC_Compiler/build/extc --run -o /tmp/should_be_written.c t_hyg.extc; echo $?
ls /tmp/should_be_written.c   # -> No such file or directory

coverage_notes: Read src/main.c (658 lines) line by line (all of it, no sampling). Covered: the file's own doc, phase timing (PHASE/nowSec/timeOn), writeFile, baseName, runCmd (fork/exec/waitpid and the exit-status contract), usage(), viewContractOk, loadPrelude (lex/parse/register/check, reserved marking, view contract, merge order), and main() in full: option parsing (-O0..-O3 validation, -march=native, -w, --dump-tokens, --dump-effects, --explain-memory, --check-c, --run, --no-line-map, -I with the 16-dir cap, -o, -h/--help, unknown-option and multi-input rejection), readWholeFile failure handling, arena/ctx/type-table setup, the lex -> dump-tokens -> prelude -> parse -> loadModules -> aliases -> module diagnostics -> check -> module body diagnostics -> codegen -> --check-c -> write/exec pipeline, and the module-context error rendering. Cross-checked and found NOT to be defects: the pipeline always renders an error before returning 1 (ctx.hasError or a module Ctx), so the `return 1` at main.c:497 is unreachable without a message in every path I could construct (missing module, unreadable module, module syntax error, import clash -- all verified to print); the --check-c temp file handling closes/unlinks on every failure path; `bufCstr` does not change the buffer length (base.c:310-314), so `fwrite(bufCstr(&c), 1, c.len, f)` writes exactly the C text; a directory passed as the input path is rejected with `extc: cannot read` (readWholeFile's fseek/ftell fails); `/dev/null` and an empty file legitimately compile (a file is a module, and `main` is not required for one); errors inside `use`d modules are rendered from the module's own Ctx before codegen (modules.c:1820-1832), which I verified with a deliberately broken module. Not reported: the known `-w`-does-not-reach-module-Ctxs gap (main.c:409, already on the Lead's list), the orphaned readWholeFile doc comment at main.c:42-56 (the function lives in base.c:599; documentation placement only), and the fact that `--dump-tokens`/`--run` ignore `-o` beyond the finding above.
